features_excluded.casualty_severity: LEAKAGE: severity of individual casualties; the collision severity is defined as the worst casualty severity. Casualty file is never loaded.
features_excluded.casualty_class: LEAKAGE/POST-EVENT: casualty-file field (describes who was hurt). Casualty file is never loaded.
features_excluded.casualty_type: LEAKAGE/POST-EVENT: casualty-file field. Casualty file is never loaded.
features_excluded.number_of_casualties: LEAKAGE: only known after the outcome, and mechanically linked to severity (a fatal collision has at least one casualty; more casualties -> more likely severe).
features_excluded.did_police_officer_attend_scene_of_accid: POST-EVENT: attendance is a response to the collision and is more likely for severe collisions, so it encodes the outcome.
features_excluded.collision_index: IDENTIFIER: no predictive meaning; kept only to de-duplicate and verify the split.
features_excluded.collision_year: Excluded to avoid memorising year-level drift (reporting changes, COVID-19 2020); kept only for analytics and temporal splitting.
features_excluded.date: Raw date replaced by engineered month / weekday / season.
features_excluded.time: Raw time replaced by engineered hour and derived flags.
features_excluded.day_of_week: Raw STATS19 code (1=Sunday) replaced by engineered weekday / is_weekend.
features_excluded.latitude: HIGH-CARDINALITY continuous geography. Not used as a model feature (location memorisation, weak generalisation); rounded copy kept for the historical map and grid aggregation only.
features_excluded.police_force: Administrative area with force-specific reporting practice; would let the model learn reporting differences rather than collision circumstances. (Move to ALLOWED_FEATURES to test it.)
features_excluded.second_road_class: Structurally missing away from junctions and largely redundant with junction_detail.

note: Cramer's V is computed on training rows only. A high value is a red flag, a low value is not proof of absence of leakage.
